chunks.arabic_text: الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ يَحْيَىٰ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ، مَوْلَىٰ الْمَنْصُورِ. رَوَىٰ عَنْ جَدِّهِ.

translations.en: Al-Qasim ibn Yahya ibn al-Hasan ibn Rashid, the client of al-Mansur. He narrated from his grandfather.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, a mawla of the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur, whose transmission from his grandfather is deemed weak, reflecting the rigorous scrutiny of isnads in early Shia scholarship. His connection to the Umayyad/Abbasid court elite underscores the political and social dynamics influencing the acceptance of narrators during the formative period of hadith compilation.
en.seo_question: Who is Al-Qasim ibn Yahya ibn al-Hasan ibn Rashid and what is his status as a narrator?

key_terms.مَوْلَىٰ: Client (mawla), referring to a freed slave or a non-Arab Muslim under the patronage of an Arab tribe or caliph.
key_terms.الْمَنْصُورُ: Al-Mansur, referring to the Abbasid Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur.
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator with less than perfect reliability or memory.
